They do not install a provider, load the owner's FontLab session or make private default resources available. Without a provider (using_info_provider(...), supplied only by tests today) the lifecycle, debug, queue, sidebar and Chinese/Hangul generation paths refuse with UnsupportedCapability; inside FontLab they are not native support claims. The matching Echopy catalogue, authored site guide and ordinary installed tuple need their own qualification for each delivery.

docs.title: Shared graph and raw accessors
docs.text: glyphInfos, name2Info and unicode2Info return the current raw index containers. setGlyphInfos_ stores the supplied object, including None, without copying it. scriptIDs, sidebarCategories, categories, subCategories and iMatraCombinations return their exact fields. The all-item, language-group, category-group and filter-group getter/setter pairs preserve identity and nil. No setter clears rank caches. _subcategoriesForSidebarCategory_(None) returns nil before requiring an initialized lifecycle; other lookups use the actual subcategory-order dictionary.

docs.title: Lazy ranking
docs.text:
indexOfObjectInScripts_ enumerates scriptIDs. indexOfObjectInCategories_ enumerates sidebarCategories, then assigns Icon, SF-Symbol, Private Use and Corner successive terminal ranks. Duplicates overwrite preceding entries. An unknown key returns 2**63 - 1. Stored indices use signed 32-bit arithmetic and return as unsigned 64-bit values.

The retained implementation tests for a nil cache before synchronizing the manager, then builds unconditionally inside that monitor. It publishes the cache before enumerating and rereads the current field for every insertion. Lookup locks the captured cache object and reads the then-current cache field. Python locks/dictionaries qualify owned models; they do not prove Foundation fast-enumeration mutation detection, key copying or NSNumber/exception ABI.

docs.title: Debug and shared construction
docs.text:
initDebug configures a fresh queue with the current active processor count, then replaces the existing name2Group dictionary. It does not allocate a second name index, load glyph data, build sidebar groups or register observers. A newly allocated owned debug receiver retains nil raw index fields. The actual base parser adopts its resulting containers on success. Missing files return false/nil; malformed qualified rows return their actual parse error. Existing lifecycle/index/local-URL/flags survive reinitialization except for the queue and group dictionary explicitly replaced by this initializer.

The shared callback preserves an existing local URL and state. Its order is new queue, current processor count, queue limit, sidebar load, glyph-info load, queue drain, observer registration. It tests the receiver observer flag's low bit and writes flag1 only after adding the current global shared receiver. Failures retain source partial state; there is no invented finally-drain. Owned NSObject identity initialization does not prove native substitution or dispatch_once ABI and lifetime behavior.

docs.title: Placeholder-font cache and observation
docs.text:
fontForScript_size_ is a class selector. Each call resolves its explicit current provider. The first nil-cache call reads ordered [script, path] rows from GSScriptToPlaceholderFontPath, creates and publishes a CF dictionary, then loads the rows. Each nonnil CGFont is stored in the current global dictionary and released after the store. Lookup retrieves the current dictionary value; a nonnil value reaches CTFontCreateWithGraphicsFont with the requested size and nil matrix/attributes. A nil value returns nil. No arbitrary fallback font or successful empty resource is invented.

The cache is global and unsynchronized in the retained source. Failed building keeps completed partial state. Invalidation drops the pointer without releasing the dictionary. The exact observed key is values.GSScriptToPlaceholderFontPath; unrelated keys do nothing. This behavior requires individual defaults/CF/CG/CT primitives. Named CF callback tokens are adapter contracts, not native pointers. CF ownership, native fonts and actual defaults resources still require a lawful adapter and native qualification.

Explicit dealloc removes the current shared observer only when the original receiver flag equals exactly1, then clears that flag after successful removal. It always dispatches the explicit super_dealloc(receiver) primitive afterward. Removal failure prevents the flag clear and superclass call. There is no Python __del__, implicit native destruction or blanket state clearing.

docs.title: Error presentation and recovery
docs.text:
reportInfoError presents GSGlyphsDomain/code1 and the retained English localized description and recovery suggestion. The owned error is an InfoError subclass; native NSError identity is unqualified. Presentation return values are discarded and exceptions propagate.

attemptRecoveryFromError_optionIndex_ preserves the source's repeated code reads. Only option1 with first code0x2ae2 or second code0x8702 reads FilePath and asks the explicit workspace primitive to reveal it. Nil paths remain nil. Other cases return true. The reveal result is ignored, but a failing reveal propagates before a successful return. No workspace or native framework is imported by these source models.

docs.title: Keep layer identity separate from its name
docs.text:
Two foreground layers can share a display name without sharing storage. Glyport keeps the declared master slots first, in font-master order, then every other valid stored foreground in native order. Mask and service records are excluded from that latter group. A missing master retains its existing pending slot; reading the collection creates no native layer or Undo entry. Without declared masters, the existing empty-collection behavior remains.

FontLab's isMasterLayer is derived from names, including interpolation/bracket names. It does not uniquely identify a declared master slot. The native case-sensitive findLayer(name) selects the last matching stored identity. Glyport uses that same finder for each declared slot and gives other same-name records their own auxiliary tokens. It does not invent persistent native metadata.

The public Glyphs-compatible isMasterLayer describes a declared slot: layer.layerId == layer.associatedMasterId. A native master-like record outside those slots is represented as an auxiliary. Imported auxiliaries without an explicit retained association keep the first-master fallback; association is separate from the displayed name and native interpolation semantics.

docs.title: Inspect every identity
docs.text:
These read-only helpers take a glyph already resolved by the caller. They do not choose a font, change selection, open a window or edit a document. The standalone checks run the exact helpers against owned primitives through the actual FontLabBackend/Model/proxy code; that is separate from native host acceptance.

def layer_rows(glyph) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    return [
        {"id": layer.layerId, "master": layer.associatedMasterId,
         "name": layer.name, "is_master": layer.isMasterLayer,
         "width": layer.width}
        for layer in glyph.layers
    ]

For example, distinct stored Regular/Bold duplicates can produce four rows with names Regular, Bold, Regular, Bold. The first two are declared slots; the last two have their own IDs. Never key a preservation snapshot by name alone.

docs.title: Select declared masters deliberately
docs.text:
def master_layers(glyph) -> list:
    return [layer for layer in glyph.layers if layer.isMasterLayer]

This intentionally selects declared slots, including a pending missing master. A zero-width pending slot is not proof that a real empty layer exists. The collection is therefore not a literal stored-only iterator for an original Transform workflow. That workflow needs its own qualified stored-layer projection, occurrence order and complete shape/component/image/anchor/PS/TT payload contract.

docs.title: Find all layers with a display name
docs.text:
def named_layers(glyph, name: str) -> list:
    return [layer for layer in glyph.layers if layer.name == name]

The result may contain several objects. glyph.layers["Regular"] is not an existing name alias: general string lookup uses exact layer IDs. Integer master ordinals and declared master IDs retain their lazy direct lookup. Other indices, slices and auxiliary IDs use the complete catalogue.

docs.title: Resolve a retained session ID
docs.text:
def layer_by_id(glyph, layer_id: str):
    return glyph.layers[layer_id]

Repeated lookup returns the same proxy while that identity remains live. Reordering or renaming an auxiliary does not merge it with another same-name record. If it becomes the finder-selected master identity, its old auxiliary handle is retired instead of silently aliasing the master slot. Removal also retires the old auxiliary/background handles. These are session tokens, not a new persistent UUID format.

The backend captures the glyph history marker when a layer handle is exposed. On a later notified history change it rebinds retained identities to replacement wrappers before reading. Unnotified native changes have no general observable history marker. Do not retry an edit blindly after a stale-handle error.

docs.title: Editing and native acceptance
docs.text:
Owned checks verify that each duplicate-layer width write changes only its exact target and that automatic-layer writes still refuse before history. Enumeration does not qualify every interpolating/generated layer for writing. Existing automatic/dependant, shared-owner, pending-update and history-scope protections remain applicable.

Actual imported layer roles/order, complete font/cache/date/lifetime preservation, Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen and all four owner-font workflows still need the native owned-fixture protocol. No API declaration or standalone model test supplies that proof. See Compatibility and the workspace acceptance ledger before treating a script as native-complete.

docs.title: Arabic presentation-form encodings
docs.text: These examples use owned offline models. They test source behaviour and do not open or modify a FontLab document. The maintained GlyphData supplies legacy presentation codes; native persistence/history and complete caller workflows still require qualification.

docs.title: Enable and refresh
docs.text:
from fly.gp.model import GSCustomParameter, GSGlyph, Model
from fly.gp.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend

KEY = "Use Arabic Presentation Form Unicodes"
font = Model(FakeBackend()).font
glyph = font.glyphs.append(GSGlyph("alef-ar"))
font.customParameters[KEY] = True
glyph.updateGlyphInfo(changeName=False)
assert glyph.name == "alef-ar"
assert glyph.unicodes == ["0627", "FE8D"]

The exact spaced key matters. The compact spelling is a different parameter. The parent font supplies the setting; a master setting does not enable it.

docs.title: First active duplicate
docs.text:
font.customParameters[KEY] = False
second = GSCustomParameter(KEY, True)
font.customParameters.append(second)
glyph.updateGlyphInfo(changeName=False)
assert glyph.unicodes == ["0627"]
font.customParameters[0].active = False
glyph.updateGlyphInfo(changeName=False)
assert glyph.unicodes == ["0627", "FE8D"]

Name assignment targets the first object, including an inactive one. Effective lookup selects the first active value. Refresh rebuilds the encoding list; it removes the earlier presentation addition when the setting becomes disabled.

docs.title: Typed values on macOS
docs.text:
from fly.gp.model.parameter_numbers import normalize
assert normalize("YES", locale_name="en_US") == 0
assert normalize("true", locale_name="en_US") == 0
assert normalize("0,5", locale_name="de_DE") == 0.5
assert normalize("0.5junk", locale_name="en_US") == float(2**63)
assert normalize("1.0e-46", locale_name="en_US") == 0.0
assert normalize(1e-46) == 1e-46

String conversion uses real NSString/NSNumberFormatter behaviour, including the current locale and float32 rounding. A failed decimal parse uses the upstream nonzero sentinel. Raw Python truthiness would get YES/true and tiny values wrong. The explicit locale above belongs to a temporary formatter; preferences remain unchanged. Normal parameter writes use the process locale and cached formatter. Numeric bool/int/float values retain precision, and typed object None becomes False. Assigning None by parameter name instead removes the first matching object.

Non-macOS string conversion and arbitrary object/container conversion explicitly raise UnsupportedCapability pending qualification. Numeric values remain usable.

docs.title: Canonical metadata and stored script
docs.text:
font = Model(FakeBackend()).font
alias = font.glyphs.append(GSGlyph("ownedArabicAlias"))
alias.unicode = "0627"
alias.storeScript = True
alias.script = "latin"
font.customParameters[KEY] = True
alias.updateGlyphInfo(changeName=False)
assert alias.name == "ownedArabicAlias" and alias.script == "latin"
assert alias.unicodes == ["0627", "FE8D"]

The presentation stage tests the resolved record's script and canonical name, then reads direct unicodeLegacy or the raw canonical .isol record. An empty non-nil legacy blocks fallback. Additions preserve order and deduplicate; generic constructed suffixes clear inherited legacy. Stored metadata overlays run later. The preceding additional-Unicode stage retains its own gates and semantics.

ROS replacement, custom managers, complete suffix synthesis and native name collision handling remain open; combined equivalence is not claimed. Requested shipped ROS maps now refuse before presentation because their proprietary data is unavailable. A native collision can clear encodings even with changeName=False. The public unicodeLegacy snapshot and its distinct global/local metadata paths are described in Legacy encodings and ROS.

docs.title: Ordered custom parameters
docs.text:
This example exercises owned offline data. It demonstrates collection behaviour; it does not qualify FontLab persistence or execute a filter.

from fly.gp.model import GSCustomParameter, Model
from fly.gp.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend

font = Model(FakeBackend()).font
first = GSCustomParameter("Filter", "First filter")
second = GSCustomParameter("Filter", "Second filter")
font.customParameters.extend([first, second])
assert font.customParameters[0] is first
assert font.customParameters["Filter"] == "First filter"
first.active = False
assert "Filter" in font.customParameters
assert font.customParameters["Filter"] == "Second filter"
font.customParameters["Filter"] = "Changed inactive filter"
assert first.value == "Changed inactive filter" and not first.active
assert font.customParameters["Filter"] == "Second filter"
font.customParameters["Filter"] = None
assert list(font.customParameters) == [second]
assert first.parent is None
second.name = "Renamed filter"
assert font.customParameters["Filter"] is None
assert font.customParameters["Renamed filter"] == "Second filter"

A name read selects the first active duplicate. A name write, name deletion or remove(parameter) acts on the first matching object, including an inactive one. Use integer indices when the intended operation is positional. Removing an object detaches it; subsequent detached edits do not change the stored collection.

Legacy lib values import without modifying unrelated data. After import, ordered records preserve duplicate names and active flags across reconstructed Python models. External additions through flat glyphsLib-compatible keys are retained. Conflicting external edits of an existing mirror raise an error before a later write can overwrite them. Full native save/reopen remains an acceptance gate.

The Arabic presentation setting requires typed numeric validation and resolver postprocessing in addition to this collection. Those stages remain pending.

For the separately packaged read-only corpus-ranking driver, set GLYPORT_ORIGINAL_CORPUS to the retained original corpus and GLYPORT_GLYPHS_WRAPPER to its pinned upstream Python wrapper. The driver parses files; it does not execute original scripts. Corpus configuration is unrelated to the owned offline example above.

docs.title: Read stored glyph descriptions
docs.text:
GSGlyphInfo.desc returns the description stored on the selected metadata record. It preserves None, empty text and Unicode text. It does not manufacture a description from a glyph name or Python's Unicode database.

In FontLab, access the public facade on the GUI thread. To share an activated session, call gp.activate() after from fly import gp and before the public import below. Outside FontLab, first call import fly.gp.GlyphsApp as gs; gs.use_backend(backend, profile="glyphs4") with an explicit backend, before accessing Glyphs. See ordinary imports and backend binding.

Query the global metadata explicitly:

from fly.gp.GlyphsApp import Glyphs

info = Glyphs.glyphInfoForName("A")
by_unicode = Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode("0041")
assert by_unicode.desc == info.desc
if info.desc:
    print(info.desc)

A suffix or compound can retain its selected seed's description. Component descriptions are not joined. Exact whole-name records can preempt composition, and Indic seed replacement can select a different record. These rules follow the existing lookup pipeline; a description read does not resolve another record.

base = Glyphs.glyphInfoForName("A")
alternate = Glyphs.glyphInfoForName("A.alt")
assert alternate.desc == base.desc

The description is read-only:

from fly.gp.errors import UnsupportedCapability

try:
    info.desc = "Replacement"
except UnsupportedCapability as error:
    assert error.capability == "GSGlyphInfo.desc"
else:
    raise AssertionError("The stored description must remain read-only")

The current provider is the versioned public GlyphData subset. A known parsed record without a description has None; an external metadata object that does not establish the field raises GSGlyphInfo.desc.source. Public subset results do not establish proprietary database completeness or every Glyphs version.

The retained wrapper and native stored getter agree with the documented GSGlyphInfo property. Current source checks cover selected-record behavior, including nullable text, aliases, Unicode, suffixes, compounds, copies and model snapshots. Matching committed artifacts, Echopy producer provenance and ordinary consumers need their separate qualification.

GSGlyph.glyphInfo selects its font/document manager. An explicit font also selects that manager for application lookup:

font = Glyphs.font
if font is not None:
    selected = Glyphs.glyphInfoForName("A", font=font)
    if selected is not None:
        print(selected.desc)

Manager hits retain canonical record views. The explicit GSGlyphInfo(glyph) constructor remains a frozen glyph snapshot; it is a different operation. Complete local initialization/reload, private resources, original scripts and native workflows remain open. Source checks do not qualify UI effects, FontLab history or saved/reopened artifacts.

docs.title: Legacy encodings and ROS metadata
docs.text:
GSGlyphInfo.unicodeLegacy reads a separate legacy encoding from maintained GlyphData. It never replaces unicode. The package exposes an owned read-only snapshot; native Glyph Info has a setter which this facade does not emulate.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.glyphsapp.application import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
info = app.glyphInfoForName("alef-ar.isol")
assert info.name == "alef-ar.isol"
assert info.unicode is None
assert info.unicodeLegacy == "FE8D"
alias = app.glyphInfoForName("aleffinalarabic")
assert alias.name == "alef-ar.fina" and alias.unicodeLegacy == "FE8E"
assert app.glyphInfoForName("alef-ar").unicodeLegacy is None

Global lookup ignores the active font, its parameters and stored overrides. Explicit non-None font lookup remains unsupported for name strings. The new global Unicode lookup indexes primary then legacy values for each public record in file order, with last-write precedence. Legacy lookup preserves the separate fields: FE8D selects alef-ar.isol, whose unicode is None and unicodeLegacy is FE8D. Integer name lookup dispatches to that method before dropping its font argument, as in the wrapper.

The retained base parser constructs this combined index. The earlier primary-only description was incorrect; historical artifact evidence remains unchanged and does not qualify this source correction. Public data is not proof of proprietary database completeness, and font-local custom loaders remain open.

Direct construction from a package GSGlyph reads the new legacy field through the owned metadata resolver. Existing name, primary encoding, script and case snapshot behavior is preserved. A nil resolved record yields no legacy encoding; it does not infer one from the glyph name or primary encoding. Generic derived suffixes clear inherited legacy metadata.

from fly.gp.model import GSGlyph
from fly.gp.glyphsapp.glyph_info import GSGlyphInfo

glyph = GSGlyph("alef-ar.isol")
info = GSGlyphInfo(glyph)
assert info.unicodeLegacy == "FE8D" and glyph.unicodes == []
glyph.name = "alef-ar.isol.owned"
assert info.unicodeLegacy == "FE8D"  # Existing snapshot stays unchanged.
assert GSGlyphInfo(glyph).unicodeLegacy is None

ROS processing in the audited upstream shared manager replaces the complete ordered Unicode set by the resolved metadata name, after additional encodings and before Arabic presentation processing. It depends on five proprietary MapFiles. They are not bundled with Glyport, and Adobe CMaps or GlyphData are not equivalent substitutes. Requests for Adobe-CNS1, Adobe-GB1, Adobe-Japan1, Adobe-KR or Adobe-Korea1 therefore raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData before metadata writes, even if the requested glyph might be absent from that map.

from fly.gp.errors import UnsupportedCapability
from fly.gp.model import Model
from fly.gp.model.fake_backend import FakeBackend

font = Model(FakeBackend()).font
glyph = font.glyphs["A"]
before = (glyph.name, glyph.unicodes)
font.customParameters["ROS"] = "Adobe-Japan1-7"
try:
    glyph.updateGlyphInfo(changeName=False)
except UnsupportedCapability as error:
    assert error.capability == "GSGlyphInfo.ROS.mappingData"
else:
    raise AssertionError("Missing ROS data must refuse")
assert (glyph.name, glyph.unicodes) == before

The guard recognizes the shared manager's exact strings: split on -; only if the count differs from three, retry using comma plus one space. The first two pieces identify the map; the supplement is ignored without numeric validation. Case and whitespace are preserved. Nil, malformed strings and names absent from the audited shipped resources leave the preceding metadata unchanged. This is the shipped shared-manager boundary, not arbitrary custom-manager equivalence. Nontext values require Objective-C description conversion and explicitly raise GSGlyphInfo.ROS.value until that conversion is qualified. Normal first-active parameter selection applies; inactive or shadowed ROS records are not selected.

No native applications are called by these examples. Full ROS mapping, custom managers, native collision handling, Undo/Redo and saved/reopened workflows remain unqualified. See Arabic presentation for the following stage and its separate platform boundaries.

docs.title: Stored production metadata
docs.text:
GSGlyphInfo.productionName preserves a known stored value: None, empty text, or explicit text, including a value equal to the nice name. The retained Glyphs4 getter reads that field directly. The adjacent public API prose is not an authority for changing a measured equal-name result to None.

Global exact names and aliases fill a nil stored field through the audited manager helper. Empty text is present and bypasses that fill. Direct Unicode queries do not fill it. A returned raw handle can observe later name access; a copy keeps the value at copy time. For a reviewed Glyport session with Glyphs imported from GlyphsApp:

from copy import copy
raw = Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode("0041")
before = copy(raw)
old_value = before.productionName
named = Glyphs.glyphInfoForName("A")
assert named.productionName == "A"
assert raw.productionName == "A"
assert before.productionName == old_value

The initial value can already be filled by earlier lookups. A uni/u-style single-record name is a copy of raw Unicode metadata; a bare character uses raw Unicode access. Synthesized direct Unicode metadata explicitly stores its constructed name. The helper's export-name normalization is separate from the stored getter: it does not rewrite an existing raw production field.

The maintained data adapter reconstructs the retained parser's single name index in record order: name, production unless it starts with lowercase uni, then alternate names normalized by the maintained public loader. Later entries win, including collisions with earlier primary names. Exact stored uni-looking names still preempt Unicode decoding; an excluded production alias alone does not.

Model results share the field until a native copy branch applies: private-use rename, additional Unicode, Arabic presentation or an enabled stored metadata flag. An equal stored overlay still copies. Arabic additional-Unicode lookup can fill the isolated record; presentation lookup stays raw. Generic suffix production appends the original suffix tokens to helper output; global base lookup and font-base resolution keep different fill behavior.

This qualifies represented public records and owned source controls. Public XML is a versioned subset, not proprietary GlyphData completeness. Complex uni/suffix/ligature and special synthesis, custom/global/font-local managers, remaining resource/version branches and complete original workflows remain open. Library-constructed classification alone cannot establish production; that getter refuses with GSGlyphInfo.productionName.source rather than invent None or a sanitized export name. Glyph production setters/storage flags and Glyphs.productionGlyphName are separate contracts and are not added here. Source tests do not establish FontLab history, persistence or native acceptance.

docs.title: Global Unicode Glyph Info
docs.text:
The private candidate implements Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode(String, font=None) and integer dispatch from glyphInfoForName. It returns the existing read-only GSGlyphInfo snapshot or None. Lookup indexes maintained public GlyphData records in file order, inserting each primary encoding and then its legacy encoding. Later records overwrite earlier keys. The separate unicode and unicodeLegacy fields retain their exact stored values; a legacy lookup does not assign that key to the primary field.

The retained Glyphs4 base parser at 002152e4 inserts legacy encodings into the same dictionary as primary encodings; loader 0022fffc passes it to the global manager. This corrects the earlier primary-only description. Public glyphsLib 6.16.2 data adds 730 legacy keys to 71,401 primary keys, for 72,131 combined keys. The duplicate legacy key 0000 selects the later NULL record. This source correction awaits fresh ordinary artifacts, consumer and native qualification; previous artifact reports describe the earlier implementation.

The executable wrapper's keyword is String, with capital S. The documentation label Unicode is not a keyword alias. These examples use an owned application fixture outside FontLab; they do not activate a native application or synthetic GlyphsApp module.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode(65).name == "A"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode(String="004a").name == "J"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("00C1").name == "Aacute"
assert [part.name for part in app.glyphInfoForUnicode("00C1").components] == [
    "A", "acutecomb"]
info = app.glyphInfoForUnicode("FE8D")
assert (info.name, info.unicode, info.unicodeLegacy) == ("alef-ar.isol", None, "FE8D")
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("FE80").name == "hamza-ar.isol"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0000").name == "NULL"

Global lookup never consults the active font, glyph state, ROS, presentation parameters or stored metadata. An explicit non-None font on the Unicode method refuses with Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.localData: a font-local manager remains unimplemented. The name method first dispatches integers to the Unicode method, discarding its font argument exactly as the audited Python wrapper does.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.errors import UnsupportedCapability
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

class UnreadableFont:
    def __getattribute__(self, name):
        raise AssertionError("Global lookup must not read the active font")

font = UnreadableFont()
app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=font), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
assert app.glyphInfoForName(65, font=font).name == "A"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0041", font=None).name == "A"
try:
    app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0041", font=font)
except UnsupportedCapability as error:
    assert error.capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode.localData"
else:
    raise AssertionError("Explicit local Unicode lookup must refuse")

docs.title: Preserve lookup spelling and synthesis
docs.text:
Nil or input shorter than three UTF-16 code units returns None before lookup. Otherwise the uppercased original text is used as the exact combined index key. There is no trimming, zero-padding or scalar canonicalization. Integer inputs, including bool and integer subclasses, first use the wrapper's exact %04X formatting. Formatting width is a minimum, not a range check.

On an index miss, the retained manager synthesizes metadata using the uppercase text for its name and encoding. The parsed 32-bit value selects the uni or u prefix and classification; it does not reformat the text. A synthesized encoding is retained only for uppercase text lengths1–7. Longer text may yield a record whose unicode is None.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
for text, name, code in [
    ("041", "uni041", "041"),
    ("000041", "uni000041", "000041"),
    ("00000041", "uni00000041", None),
    ("0FE8D", "uni0FE8D", "0FE8D"),
]:
    info = app.glyphInfoForUnicode(text)
    assert (info.name, info.unicode, info.unicodeLegacy) == (name, code, None)
assert app.glyphInfoForName("alef-ar.isol").unicodeLegacy == "FE8D"

The historical hex helper skips ASCII spaces and minus signs, treats any minus as final negation, adds nibbles with shift counts modulo32 and wraps sums to32bits. Invalid text returns its sentinel, which the manager rejects. Signed high-bit values take the BMP naming route; 10FFFE is accepted and 10FFFF is rejected. This reproduces source behavior rather than applying a strict Unicode-scalar validator. Reading these snapshots does not assign malformed encodings to fonts.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
for text in ("--41", " 4 1 ", "   "):
    info = app.glyphInfoForUnicode(text)
    assert info.name == "uni" + text and info.unicode == text
for text in ("80000000", "100000000", "FFFFFFFFF"):
    info = app.glyphInfoForUnicode(text)
    assert info.name == "uni" + text and info.unicode is None
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("10FFFE").name == "u10FFFE"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("10FFFF") is None
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("U+0041") is None

Synthesized case is0, subCategory and unicodeLegacy are None. PUA uses category Private Use with no script. Otherwise the audited historical Han ranges yield script han and category Letter; other synthesized records use Other. These are specific source ranges, not current Unicode Script inference. Direct maintained records retain their own metadata and supported NFD components.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("00ﬀ").name == "ydieresis"  # Uppercase expands to00FF.
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0ﬀ") is None  # Minimum length checked before expansion.
info = app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0009FCC")  # Seven-digit spelling forces synthesis.
assert (info.script, info.category) == ("han", "Letter")
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("0009FCD").category == "Other"
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("00F8FF").category == "Private Use"

docs.title: Explicit boundaries
docs.text:
Only built-in strings, None and wrapper-dispatched integers are supported. Other bridge types, including string subclasses, refuse explicitly without broad string/integer coercion. Non-None font refusal precedes payload checks. An actual malformed UTF-16 string can make Foundation's native UTF8String return NULL; the retained helper dereferences that pointer unchecked. This package refuses that unsafe domain. Hex text D800 is a distinct, supported synthesis input.

from types import SimpleNamespace
from fly.gp.errors import UnsupportedCapability
from fly.gp.glyphsapp import GSApplication

app = GSApplication(SimpleNamespace(font=None), object(), {}, None, lambda *args: None)
for value, capability in [([], "inputType"), ("\ud80000", "UTF16")]:
    try:
        app.glyphInfoForUnicode(value)
    except UnsupportedCapability as error:
        assert error.capability == "Glyphs.glyphInfoForUnicode." + capability
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Unqualified or unsafe bridge input must refuse")
assert app.glyphInfoForUnicode("D800").unicode == "D800"

Standalone macOS27.2 Foundation calibration covered all1,112,064valid scalars: Python3.11 uppercase differs for55, but only non-ASCII ﬀ enters the accepted parser alphabet, identically in both. This scopes the measured casing boundary; it does not qualify other Foundation versions or arbitrary PyObjC conversion. Maintained GlyphData is not proof of proprietary database identity/completeness. Custom/global overlays, font-local managers, remaining Glyph Info fields and native workflows remain open. See legacy/ROS for the separate font-local postprocessing boundary.
